items.answer: Data analysts typically spend their days pulling data using SQL, cleaning and exploring it for patterns, building charts and dashboards, and writing up their findings along with recommendations. A significant portion of their time is also dedicated to clarifying questions and verifying that the data can be trusted.

Core skills for a frontend developer include HTML, CSS, JavaScript, TypeScript, and a component framework such as React. Important supporting skills involve accessibility, responsive layout, calling HTTP APIs, version control with Git, browser developer tools, and component testing.

To get started in UX design, learn the fundamentals of usability and practise on real problems. You can pick an everyday app, test it with three people, and redesign one flow based on what you observed. Your portfolio should highlight your process and reasoning, including any changes made after testing, rather than just final screens.

A data analyst focuses on explaining what has happened using SQL, descriptive statistics, and visualization to help decision makers. A data scientist focuses more on prediction and experimentation, utilizing statistics and machine learning for modeling and handling uncertainty.

UX design focuses on how a product works, including steps, structure, and task completion, while UI design focuses on the visual and interactive surface, such as layout, type, colour, and components. People who enjoy research and problem framing tend towards UX, whereas those who enjoy visual craft and detail tend towards UI.

A DevOps engineer builds and maintains the systems that transition software from a developer's machine to reliable production operation. Their day-to-day work involves maintaining build and deployment pipelines, managing cloud infrastructure as code, setting up monitoring and alerts, responding to incidents, and automating repetitive manual work.

Core skills for a machine learning engineer include strong software engineering in Python, machine learning fundamentals, a deep learning framework, and model evaluation. Important supporting skills are data pipelines, deployment with containers and cloud services, monitoring, and for language-model applications, prompt design, retrieval and systematic evaluation.

To get started as a backend developer, pick one language and build a small API with a real database where you create, read, update, and delete records, and then add a login feature. You should learn SQL properly rather than relying only on libraries, deploy the project, add tests, and practice explaining your design choices.
QA engineers frequently transition into test automation engineering, backend development, DevOps, or product roles.

A product designer is responsible for taking a feature from the initial understanding of a problem all the way to the final interface, combining user experience design, user interface design, and an understanding of product and business needs.

To get started as a UX researcher, practise core methods on a small scale by interviewing five people about a task, running a usability test on an app, and writing a short report separating observations from conclusions. Learning to ask about past behaviour instead of opinions is an early key skill.
A data engineer builds the pipelines and storage that move data from where it is created to where analysts, data scientists and applications can use it.
People who enjoy visual craft and detail, such as typography, colour and layout, tend towards UI design, which focuses on the visual and interactive surface of a product.

Frontend development focuses on user interfaces, design detail, and accessibility, while backend development involves APIs, business logic, and data storage. Both paths require programming fundamentals, Git, and testing. To find your preference, the most reliable method is trying a small project of each kind.

Treat your assessment score as a starting point rather than a verdict since it is only an estimate from a small number of questions. Review the topic breakdown to identify weaker areas, read the explanations for missed questions, and select one or two topics to study before attempting the assessment again. While a higher score in a specific domain indicates that related roles may fit your current skills, your interest and practice are just as important as the score itself.

A mobile developer needs to learn core skills including Kotlin for Android, Swift for iOS, or a cross-platform framework like Flutter or React Native. Important supporting skills involve interface layout, state management, working with APIs, local storage, platform design guidelines, and debugging on real devices.
Site reliability engineering is a closely related role to a DevOps engineer that focuses on keeping services available and fast.

A software tester, or QA engineer, performs daily work that includes designing test cases from requirements, conducting exploratory testing of new features, writing and maintaining automated tests, reporting bugs clearly with reproduction steps, and verifying that fixed bugs remain fixed.
Data analysts often move towards data science by adding programming in Python, machine learning, and deeper statistics.

To get started as a UI designer, study visual fundamentals and practise by rebuilding well-made interfaces to understand their spacing and type. Next, design a small set of components with all their states and use them to assemble a few screens, making sure to check contrast and keyboard focus from the beginning.
A data engineer builds pipelines and storage to move data, and models tables in a data warehouse.
Data scientists design and analyse experiments such as A/B tests as part of their typical day-to-day work.
A UX design portfolio should display your process and reasoning, including what you changed after testing, rather than only presenting the final screens.
A machine learning engineer builds applications on large language models that include retrieval and evaluation.
Yes, SQL is a core skill for a data analyst and is used for pulling data as part of their day-to-day work. It is also recommended as the first skill to learn when getting started in the role.
Backend developers often grow into full-stack development, DevOps and site reliability work, or data engineering.

A backend developer needs to know core skills including one server-side language such as Java, Python, Go, or JavaScript, along with relational databases and SQL, HTTP and API design, and data structures and algorithms.

Typical work for a UX designer includes talking to users, mapping user flows, sketching wireframes, building prototypes, running usability tests, and refining designs based on what is learned. UX designers also work closely with product managers and developers throughout the process.

To get started as a data engineer, you should become very good at SQL and comfortable in Python. You can begin by building a small pipeline that pulls data from a public API on a schedule, cleans it, loads it into a database, and checks its quality. Additionally, learning how to model tables for analysis is just as important as learning the necessary tools.

Frontend developers often move towards full-stack development by learning backend skills, or towards design engineering and UI design by deepening visual and interaction skills. Mobile development is also a close neighbour due to shared interface thinking.
A QA engineer, or software tester, finds problems before users do and helps a team build quality into its process. The role covers planning what to test, testing by hand, and writing automated tests.

To become a data scientist, you should build a base in statistics and probability, Python with data libraries, SQL, and machine learning methods together with honest model evaluation. Important supporting skills include experiment design, data visualisation, and communicating uncertainty clearly.

A UX designer shapes how a product works by focusing on user steps, information organisation, and usability through research, wireframing, and testing. A product designer takes responsibility for a feature from the initial problem understanding to the final interface, combining UX design, UI design, and a broader view of product and business needs.

A UX researcher studies product users to help teams make evidence-based decisions rather than relying on assumptions. Their day-to-day work includes planning research with clear questions, recruiting participants, conducting interviews and usability tests, designing surveys, analysing results, and presenting findings and their limits to designers, product managers, and engineers.

Core skills for a DevOps engineer include Linux, networking fundamentals, scripting, continuous integration and delivery, containers, and at least one cloud platform. Important supporting skills consist of infrastructure as code, monitoring and logging, security basics, and calm, systematic troubleshooting.

To get started in mobile app development, choose one platform and build a simple complete app, like a notes or expense tracker that saves data locally. Next, add a network call and handle situations where the network is unavailable. Publishing even a small application will teach you the full release process.
Data engineers often transition into analytics engineering, machine learning engineering, or data platform and architecture roles.

A UI designer works on designing screens and components, defining styles for type, colour and spacing, specifying states like hover, focus, error and loading, maintaining a design system, and collaborating with developers to ensure the built result matches the design.
